newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian soybean prices firm on slow arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Indian soybean prices firm on slow arrivals.

text.p: Indian soybean prices firmed during the week as farmers held back stocks in the hope of selling later at higher prices, traders said on Friday.
Arrivals fell to 800 tonnes per day, compared with 12,000 tonnes at the same time last year, in the markets of central India at the hub of the country's soybean industry.
Soybeans were quoted at 13,200 to 13,400 rupees per tonne compared with 10,800 to 11,100 rupees at the same time last year.
"Soybean trading was very limited," said Prakash Vohra, a leading oilmeal broker. "Availability was poor and processing plants don't have much stocks."
Traders said export demand for Indian soy meal was dull. Soy meal for export was quoted at $318-$319 per tonne FAS, against around $225 a year ago.
